look_here_first: FIRST LOOK FOR SMALL ROUNDED HEADS, NOT A RED SPOT. Graceful sandmat (Euphorbia hypericifolia) is a GLABROUS upright-to-ascending annual whose tiny cyathia gather in DENSE TERMINAL AND AXILLARY HEADLIKE GLOMERULES with short/reduced bracts. Its opposite oblong leaves are mostly hairless and often finely toothed near the apex. At the nodes look for relatively large reddish TRIANGULAR stipule scales; FNA describes them as joined (connate), generally 1.5–2.2 mm, but the current photos prove their presence/shape better than the precise two-sided fusion seam. Compare E. nutans (leafier loose cyathial clusters, frequently short incurved stem hairs) and E. hyssopifolia (usually less compact/leafier reproductive clusters, smaller stipules). Smooth fruit alone is insufficient because all three may have glabrous fruit. Mature detached seed and definitive scaled smooth capsule macros still needed; nativity-by-county badge is NOT being promoted.
photo_note: FIVE CC BY or equivalent licensed exact-species physically saved photographs (one Duarte Frade iNaturalist, four M108t Wikimedia Commons) with THIRTEEN structure arrows already saved and reviewed. Source pixel review of both magnified stipule-position photographs completed October 21: reddish triangular stipule-like projections are visible at the nodes, but neither the exact 1.5–2.2mm size nor the fully connate connection is calibrated. Public image rights acceptable with attribution. Remaining scientifically meaningful photo gaps: measured mature 3-lobed smooth capsule, loose mature seed with surface sculpture, whole rooted plant with scale, and true same-node two-side stipule-fusion demonstration.

taxonomic_note: Accepted Euphorbia hypericifolia L. in POWO and Flora of North America. Not to be confused with E. hyssopifolia or the historically misapplied E. nutans complex; do not substitute garden cultivar 'Diamond Frost' photographs for wild plants.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbiaceae; Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum: opposite unequal leaves, milky latex, cyathium (tiny special flower head), dry three-lobed capsule.
morphology_keys.habit: Annual taprooted herb; ascending/erect, 15–50 cm; shoots glabrous. New habit photograph is a potential example, not calibrated proof of height.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite, obliquely oblong to oblanceolate, 10–35 × 7–15 mm, asymmetric base, margins serrate/serrulate especially distally, glabrous; petioles 1–3 mm.
morphology_keys.stipules: Paired stipules at nodes fused into deltoid, usually entire scales (occasionally fringed apically), 1.5–2.2 mm, glabrous; often spreading away from stem. Need both-side node photo and scale before arrow labeling exact fusion.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Cyathia crowded in dense, axillary or terminal headlike clusters (glomerules), with much-reduced bractlike leaves, NOT the leafy loosely spaced small cymes of E. nutans or E. hyssopifolia.
morphology_keys.cyathium: Four yellow-green/brown, often stipitate glands; white-pink petal-like gland appendages may be inconspicuous or absent from smaller glands. These are not true petals.
morphology_keys.seed: About 0.9–1.1 × 0.5 mm; pale brown underneath a thin white mucilage coat; low smooth ridges and shallow irregular pits/depressions, not the 2–3 conspicuous transverse bars often seen in E. hyssopifolia.
best_field_traits: dense terminal and axillary glomerules of many tiny cyathia
small, highly reduced bracts at cyathium heads
hairless stems and leaf surfaces (verify at basal node, not only at tips)
fused triangular nodal stipules about 1.5–2.2 mm
asymmetric opposite oblong leaves with finely serrate margins
seed sculpture if mature, with scale and confirmed exact species

comparisons.key_distinctions: Hypericifolia has glabrous stems AND dense head-like cyathia clusters with reduced bracts plus larger fused triangular stipules; hyssopifolia has generally smaller/leafier clusters and 0.5-1 mm lacerate stipules; nutans usually bears crinkled stem hairs and less condensed leafy cymes. Smooth capsules alone do not separate these species.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: DENSE ROUNDED CYATHIUM HEADS + SMOOTH STEMS
steps: Look for the head-shaped clusters of many tiny cyathia at terminal and axillary short branches; don't call the entire round group one flower or fruit.
Locate opposite paired relatively broad green leaves on hairless stems, often with tiny apical marginal teeth.
At 10×–20× find the large pink-to-red triangular scales beside opposite leaf bases. Confirm actual stipule join from two angles if possible; current photos show location, NOT measured fusion extent.
Compare nodding spurge (E. nutans): its cyathia are generally solitary or small leafy clusters and stems may have short incurved hairs at nodes.
Compare E. hyssopifolia: it has smaller usually fringed/lacerate stipules and less condensed/leafier cymes; do not use one solitary head as species proof.
To finish the microscopic key, photograph a smooth mature 3-lobed capsule with ruler and the true detached 4-angled seed: FNA describes shallow irregular pits alternating with low ridges.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: The five saved photos resolve flowers, opposite leaves and stipule LOCATIONS, not both-sided fusion at an accurately measured scale. The seed and mature fruit surfaces must be shown with additional exact-species licensed photos. Project county nativity remains unaudited.
